text: And as they were seeking to kill him, a representation came to the chiliarch of the band that the whole of Jerusalem was in a tumult;

title: Acts 21:32
text: who, taking with him immediately soldiers and centurions, ran down upon them. But they, seeing the chiliarch and the soldiers, ceased beating Paul.

title: Acts 21:33
text: Then the chiliarch came up and laid hold upon him, and commanded [him] to be bound with two chains, and inquired who he might be, and what he had done.

title: Acts 21:34
text: And different persons cried some different thing in the crowd. But he, not being able to know the certainty on account of the uproar, commanded him to be brought into the fortress.

title: Acts 21:35
text: But when he got upon the stairs it was so that he was borne by the soldiers on account of the violence of the crowd.

title: Acts 21:36
text: For the multitude of the people followed, crying, Away with him.

title: Acts 21:37
text: But as he was about to be led into the fortress, Paul says to the chiliarch, Is it allowed me to say something to thee? And he said, Dost thou know Greek?

title: Acts 21:38
text: Thou art not then that Egyptian who before these days raised a sedition and led out into the wilderness the four thousand men of the assassins?

title: Acts 21:39
text: But Paul said, *I* am a Jew of Tarsus, citizen of no insignificant city of Cilicia, and I beseech of thee, allow me to speak to the people.

title: Acts 21:40
text: And when he had allowed him, Paul, standing on the stairs, beckoned with his hand to the people; and a great silence having been made, he addressed them in the Hebrew tongue, saying,

title: Acts 22:1
text: ¶Brethren and fathers, hear my defence which I now make to you.

title: Acts 22:2
text: And hearing that he addressed them in the Hebrew tongue, they kept the more quiet; and he says,

title: Acts 22:3
text: ¶*I* am a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, but brought up in this city, at the feet of Gamaliel, educated according to [the] exactness of the law of [our] fathers, being zealous for God, as *ye* are all this day;

title: Acts 22:4
text: who have persecuted this way unto death, binding and delivering up to prisons both men and women;

title: Acts 22:5
text: as also the high priest bears me witness, and all the elderhood: from whom also, having received letters to the brethren, I went to Damascus to bring those also who were there, bound, to Jerusalem, to be punished.

title: Acts 22:6
text: And it came to pass, as I was journeying and drawing near to Damascus, that, about mid-day, there suddenly shone out of heaven a great light round about me.

title: Acts 22:7
text: And I fell to the ground, and heard a voice saying to me, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

title: Acts 22:8
text: And *I* answered, Who art thou, Lord? And he said to me, *I* am Jesus the Nazaraean, whom *thou* persecutest.

title: Acts 22:9
text: But they that were with me beheld the light, [and were filled with fear], but heard not the voice of him that was speaking to me.

title: Acts 22:10
text: And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said to me, Rise up, and go to Damascus, and there it shall be told thee of all things which it is appointed thee to do.

title: Acts 22:11
text: And as I could not see, through the glory of that light, being led by the hand of those who were with me, I came to Damascus.

title: Acts 22:12
text: And a certain Ananias, a pious man according to the law, borne witness to by all the Jews who dwelt [there],

title: Acts 22:13
text: coming to me and standing by me, said to me, Brother Saul, receive thy sight. And *I*, in the same hour, received my sight and saw him.

title: Acts 22:14
text: And he said, The God of our fathers has chosen thee beforehand to know his will, and to see the just one, and to hear a voice out of his mouth;

title: Acts 22:15
text: for thou shalt be a witness for him to all men of what thou hast seen and heard.

title: Acts 22:16
text: And now why lingerest thou? Arise and get baptised, and have thy sins washed away, calling on his name.

title: Acts 22:17
text: And it came to pass when I had returned to Jerusalem, and as I was praying in the temple, that I became in ecstasy,

title: Acts 22:18
text: and saw him saying to me, Make haste and go quickly out of Jerusalem, for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.

title: Acts 22:19
text: And *I* said, Lord, they themselves know that *I* was imprisoning and beating in every synagogue those that believe on thee;

title: Acts 22:20
text: and when the blood of thy witness Stephen was shed, I also myself was standing by and consenting, and kept the clothes of them who killed him.

title: Acts 22:21
text: And he said to me, Go, for *I* will send thee to the nations afar off.

title: Acts 22:22
text: ¶And they heard him until this word, and lifted up their voice, saying, Away with such a one as that from the earth, for it was not fit he should live.

title: Acts 22:23
text: And as they were crying, and throwing away their clothes, and casting dust into the air,

title: Acts 22:24
text: the chiliarch commanded him to be brought into the fortress, saying that he should be examined by scourging, that he might ascertain for what cause they cried thus against him.

title: Acts 22:25
text: But as they stretched him forward with the thongs, Paul said to the centurion who stood [by], Is it lawful for you to scourge a man [who is] a Roman and uncondemned?

title: Acts 22:26
text: And the centurion, having heard it, went and reported it to the chiliarch, saying, What art thou going to do? for this man is a Roman.

title: Acts 22:27
text: And the chiliarch coming up said to him, Tell me, Art *thou* a Roman? And he said, Yes.

title: Acts 22:28
text: And the chiliarch answered, *I*, for a great sum, bought this citizenship. And Paul said, But *I* was also [free] born.

title: Acts 22:29
text: Immediately therefore those who were going to examine him left him, and the chiliarch also was afraid when he ascertained that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.

title: Acts 22:30
text: And on the morrow, desirous to know the certainty [of the matter] why he was accused of the Jews, he loosed him, and commanded the chief priests and all the council to meet, and having brought Paul down set him before them.

title: Acts 23:1
text: ¶And Paul, fixing his eyes on the council, said, Brethren, I have walked in all good conscience with God unto this day.

title: Acts 23:2
text: But the high priest Ananias ordered those standing by him to smite his mouth.

title: Acts 23:3
text: Then Paul said to him, God will smite thee, whited wall. And *thou*, dost thou sit judging me according to the law, and breaking the law commandest me to be smitten?

title: Acts 23:4
text: And those that stood by said, Dost thou rail against the high priest of God?

title: Acts 23:5
text: And Paul said, I was not conscious, brethren, that he was high priest; for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evilly of the ruler of thy people.

title: Acts 23:6
text: ¶But Paul, knowing that the one part [of them] were of the Sadducees and the other of the Pharisees, cried out in the council, Brethren, *I* am a Pharisee, son of Pharisees: *I* am judged concerning the hope and resurrection of [the] dead.

title: Acts 23:7
text: And when he had spoken this, there was a tumult of the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the multitude was divided.

title: Acts 23:8
text: For Sadducees say there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit; but Pharisees confess both of them.

title: Acts 23:9
text: And there was a great clamour, and the scribes of the Pharisees' part rising up contended, saying, We find nothing evil in this man; and if a spirit has spoken to him, or an angel...

title: Acts 23:10
text: And a great tumult having arisen, the chiliarch, fearing lest Paul should have been torn in pieces by them, commanded the troop to come down and take him by force from the midst of them, and to bring [him] into the fortress.

title: Acts 23:11
text: But the following night the Lord stood by him, and said, Be of good courage; for as thou hast testified the things concerning me at Jerusalem, so thou must bear witness at Rome also.

title: Acts 23:12
text: ¶And when it was day, the Jews, having banded together, put themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink till they should kill Paul.

title: Acts 23:13
text: And they were more than forty who had joined together in this oath;

title: Acts 23:14
text: and they went to the chief priests and elders, and said, We have cursed ourselves with a curse to taste nothing until we kill Paul.

title: Acts 23:15
text: Now therefore do ye with the council make a representation to the chiliarch so that he may bring him down to you, as about to determine more precisely what concerns him, and we, before he draws near, are ready to kill him.

title: Acts 23:16
text: But Paul's sister's son, having heard of the lying in wait, came and entered into the fortress and reported [it] to Paul.

title: Acts 23:17
text: And Paul, having called one of the centurions, said, Take this youth to the chiliarch, for he has something to report to him.

title: Acts 23:18
text: He therefore, having taken him with [him], led him to the chiliarch, and says, The prisoner Paul called me to [him] and asked me to lead this youth to thee, who has something to say to thee.

title: Acts 23:19
text: And the chiliarch having taken him by the hand, and having gone apart in private, inquired, What is it that thou hast to report to me?

title: Acts 23:20
text: And he said, The Jews have agreed together to make a request to thee, that thou mayest bring Paul down to-morrow into the council, as about to inquire something more precise concerning him.

title: Acts 23:21
text: Do not thou then be persuaded by them, for there lie in wait for him of them more than forty men, who have put themselves under a curse neither to eat nor drink till they kill him; and now they are ready waiting the promise from thee.

title: Acts 23:22
text: The chiliarch then dismissed the youth, commanding [him], Utter to no one that thou hast represented these things to me.

title: Acts 23:23
text: And having called to [him] certain two of the centurions, he said, Prepare two hundred soldiers that they may go as far as Caesarea, and seventy horsemen, and two hundred light-armed footmen, for the third hour of the night.

title: Acts 23:24
text: And [he ordered them] to provide beasts, that they might set Paul on them and carry [him] safe through to Felix the governor,

title: Acts 23:25
text: having written a letter, couched in this form:

title: Acts 23:26
text: Claudius Lysias to the most excellent governor Felix, greeting.

title: Acts 23:27
text: This man, having been taken by the Jews, and being about to be killed by them, I came up with the military and took out [of their hands], having learned that he was a Roman.

title: Acts 23:28
text: And desiring to know the charge on which they accused him, I brought him down to their council;

title: Acts 23:29
text: whom I found to be accused of questions of their law, but to have no charge laid against him [making him] worthy of death or of bonds.

title: Acts 23:30
text: But having received information of a plot about to be put in execution against the man [by the Jews], I have immediately sent him to thee, commanding also his accusers to say before thee the things that are against him. [Farewell.]

title: Acts 23:31
text: The soldiers therefore, according to what was ordered them, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris,

title: Acts 23:32
text: and on the morrow, having left the horsemen to go with him, returned to the fortress.

title: Acts 23:33
text: And these, having entered into Caesarea, and given up the letter to the governor, presented Paul also to him.

title: Acts 23:34
text: And having read [it], and asked of what eparchy he was, and learned that [he was] of Cilicia,

title: Acts 23:35
text: he said, I will hear thee fully when thine accusers also are arrived. And he commanded him to be kept in Herod's praetorium.

title: Acts 24:1
text: ¶And after five days came down the high priest Ananias, with the elders, and a certain orator called Tertullus, and laid their informations against Paul before the governor.

title: Acts 24:2
text: And he having been called, Tertullus began to accuse, saying, Seeing we enjoy great peace through thee, and that excellent measures are executed for this nation by thy forethought,

title: Acts 24:3
text: we receive [it] always and everywhere, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.

title: Acts 24:4
text: But that I may not too much intrude on thy time, I beseech thee to hear us briefly in thy kindness.

title: Acts 24:5
text: For finding this man a pest, and moving sedition among all the Jews throughout the world, and a leader of the sect of the Nazaraeans;

title: Acts 24:6
text: who also attempted to profane the temple; whom we also had seized, [and would have judged according to our law;

title: Acts 24:7
text: but Lysias, the chiliarch, coming up, took [him] away with great force out of our hands,

title: Acts 24:8
text: having commanded his accusers to come to thee;] of whom thou canst thyself, in examining [him], know the certainty of all these things of which we accuse him.

title: Acts 24:9
text: And the Jews also joined in pressing the matter against [Paul], saying that these things were so.

title: Acts 24:10
text: ¶But Paul, the governor having beckoned to him to speak, answered, Knowing that for many years thou hast been judge to this nation, I answer readily as to the things which concern myself.

title: Acts 24:11
text: As thou mayest know that there are not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem,

title: Acts 24:12
text: and neither in the temple did they find me discoursing to any one, or making any tumultuous gathering together of the crowd, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city;

title: Acts 24:13
text: neither can they make good the things of which they now accuse me.

title: Acts 24:14
text: But this I avow to thee, that in the way which they call sect, so I serve my fathers' God, believing all things which are written throughout the law, and in the prophets;

title: Acts 24:15
text: having hope towards God, which they themselves also receive, that there is to be a resurrection both of just and unjust.

title: Acts 24:16
text: For this cause I also exercise [myself] to have in everything a conscience without offence towards God and men.

title: Acts 24:17
text: And after a lapse of many years I arrived, bringing alms to my nation, and offerings.

title: Acts 24:18
text: Whereupon they found me purified in the temple, with neither crowd nor tumult. But it was certain Jews from Asia,

title: Acts 24:19
text: who ought to appear before thee and accuse, if they have anything against me;

title: Acts 24:20
text: or let these themselves say what wrong they found in me when I stood before the council,

title: Acts 24:21
text: [other] than concerning this one voice which I cried standing amongst them: I am judged this day by you touching [the] resurrection of [the] dead.

title: Acts 24:22
text: ¶And Felix, knowing accurately the things concerning the way, adjourned them, saying, When Lysias the chiliarch is come down I will determine your affair;

title: Acts 24:23
text: ordering the centurion to keep him, and that he should have freedom, and to hinder none of his friends to minister to him.

title: Acts 24:24
text: And after certain days, Felix having arrived with Drusilla his wife, who was a Jewess, he sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.

title: Acts 24:25
text: And as he reasoned concerning righteousness, and temperance, and the judgment about to come, Felix, being filled with fear, answered, Go for the present, and when I get an opportunity I will send for thee;

title: Acts 24:26
text: hoping at the same time that money would be given him by Paul: wherefore also he sent for him the oftener and communed with him.

title: Acts 24:27
text: But when two years were completed, Felix was relieved by Porcius Festus as his successor; and Felix, desirous to oblige the Jews, to acquire their favour, left Paul bound.

title: Acts 25:1
text: ¶Festus therefore, being come into the eparchy, after three days went up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

title: Acts 25:2
text: And the chief priests and the chief of the Jews laid informations before him against Paul, and besought him,

title: Acts 25:3
text: asking as a grace against him that he would send for him to Jerusalem, laying people in wait to kill him on the way.

title: Acts 25:4
text: Festus therefore answered that Paul should be kept at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to set out shortly.

title: Acts 25:5
text: Let therefore the persons of authority among you, says he, going down too, if there be anything in this man, accuse him.

title: Acts 25:6
text: And having remained among them not more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea; and on the next day, having sat down on the judgment-seat, commanded Paul to be brought.

title: Acts 25:7
text: And when he was come, the Jews who were come down from Jerusalem stood round, bringing many and grievous charges which they were not able to prove:

title: Acts 25:8
text: Paul answering for himself, Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I offended [in] anything.

title: Acts 25:9
text: But Festus, desirous of obliging the Jews, to acquire their favour, answering Paul, said, Art thou willing to go up to Jerusalem, there to be judged before me concerning these things?

title: Acts 25:10
text: But Paul said, I am standing before the judgment-seat of Caesar, where I ought to be judged. To the Jews have I done no wrong, as *thou* also very well knowest.

title: Acts 25:11
text: If then I have done any wrong and committed anything worthy of death, I do not deprecate dying; but if there is nothing of those things of which they accuse me, no man can give me up to them. I appeal to Caesar.

title: Acts 25:12
text: Then Festus, having conferred with the council, answered, Thou hast appealed to Caesar. To Caesar shalt thou go.

title: Acts 25:13
text: ¶And when certain days had elapsed, Agrippa the king and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to salute Festus.

title: Acts 25:14
text: And when they had spent many days there, Festus laid before the king the matters relating to Paul, saying, There is a certain man left prisoner by Felix,

title: Acts 25:15
text: concerning whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews laid informations, requiring judgment against him:

title: Acts 25:16
text: to whom I answered, It is not [the] custom of the Romans to give up any man before that the accused have the accusers face to face, and he have got opportunity of defence touching the charge.

title: Acts 25:17
text: When therefore they had come together here, without putting it off, I sat the next day on the judgment-seat and commanded the man to be brought:

title: Acts 25:18
text: concerning whom the accusers, standing up, brought no such accusation of guilt as *I* supposed;

title: Acts 25:19
text: but had against him certain questions of their own system of worship, and concerning a certain Jesus who is dead, whom Paul affirmed to be living.

title: Acts 25:20
text: And as I myself was at a loss as to an inquiry into these things, I said, Was he willing to go to Jerusalem and there to be judged concerning these things?

title: Acts 25:21
text: But Paul having appealed to be kept for the cognisance of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept till I shall send him to Caesar.

title: Acts 25:22
text: And Agrippa [said] to Festus, I myself also would desire to hear the man. To-morrow, said he, thou shalt hear him.

title: Acts 25:23
text: On the morrow therefore, Agrippa being come, and Bernice, with great pomp, and having entered into the hall of audience, with the chiliarchs and the men of distinction of the city, and Festus having given command, Paul was brought.

title: Acts 25:24
text: And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all men who are here present with us, ye see this person, concerning whom all the multitude of the Jews applied to me both in Jerusalem and here, crying out against [him] that he ought not to live any longer.

title: Acts 25:25
text: But I, having found that he had done nothing worthy of death, and this [man] himself having appealed to Augustus, I have decided to send him;

title: Acts 25:26
text: concerning whom I have nothing certain to write to my lord. Wherefore I have brought him before you, and specially before thee, king Agrippa, so that an examination having been gone into I may have something to write:

title: Acts 25:27
text: for it seems to me senseless, sending a prisoner, not also to signify the charges against him.

title: Acts 26:1
text: ¶And Agrippa said to Paul, It is permitted thee to speak for thyself. Then Paul stretching out his hand answered in his defence:

title: Acts 26:2
text: I count myself happy, king Agrippa, in having to answer to-day before thee concerning all of which I am accused by the Jews,

title: Acts 26:3
text: especially because thou art acquainted with all the customs and questions which are among the Jews; wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.

title: Acts 26:4
text: My manner of life then from my youth, which from its commencement was passed among my nation in Jerusalem, know all the Jews,

title: Acts 26:5
text: who knew me before from the outset [of my life], if they would bear witness, that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.

title: Acts 26:6
text: And now I stand to be judged because of the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,

title: Acts 26:7
text: to which our whole twelve tribes serving incessantly day and night hope to arrive; about which hope, O king, I am accused of [the] Jews.

title: Acts 26:8
text: Why should it be judged a thing incredible in your sight if God raises the dead?

title: Acts 26:9
text: *I* indeed myself thought that I ought to do much against the name of Jesus the Nazaraean.

title: Acts 26:10
text: Which also I did in Jerusalem, and myself shut up in prisons many of the saints, having received the authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death I gave my vote.

title: Acts 26:11
text: And often punishing them in all the synagogues, I compelled them to blaspheme. And, being exceedingly furious against them, I persecuted them even to cities out [of our own land].

title: Acts 26:12
text: ¶And when, [engaged] in this, I was journeying to Damascus, with authority and power from the chief priests,

title: Acts 26:13
text: at mid-day, on the way, I saw, O king, a light above the brightness of the sun, shining from heaven round about me and those who were journeying with me.

title: Acts 26:14
text: And, when we were all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice saying to me in the Hebrew tongue, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? [it is] hard for thee to kick against goads.

title: Acts 26:15
text: And I said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, *I* am Jesus whom *thou* persecutest:

title: Acts 26:16
text: but rise up and stand on thy feet; for, for this purpose have I appeared to thee, to appoint thee to be a servant and a witness both of what thou hast seen, and of what I shall appear to thee in,

title: Acts 26:17
text: taking thee out from among the people, and the nations, to whom *I* send thee,

title: Acts 26:18
text: to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive remission of sins and inheritance among them that are sanctified by faith in me.

title: Acts 26:19
text: Whereupon, king Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision;

title: Acts 26:20
text: but have, first to those both in Damascus and Jerusalem, and to all the region of Judaea, and to the nations, announced that they should repent and turn to God, doing works worthy of repentance.

title: Acts 26:21
text: On account of these things the Jews, having seized me in the temple, attempted to lay hands on and destroy me.

title: Acts 26:22
text: Having therefore met with [the] help which is from God, I have stood firm unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying nothing else than those things which both the prophets and Moses have said should happen,

title: Acts 26:23
text: [namely,] whether Christ should suffer; whether he first, through resurrection of [the] dead, should announce light both to the people and to the nations.

title: Acts 26:24
text: ¶And as he answered for his defence with these things, Festus says with a loud voice, Thou art mad, Paul; much learning turns thee to madness.

title: Acts 26:25
text: But Paul said, I am not mad, most excellent Festus, but utter words of truth and soberness;

title: Acts 26:26
text: for the king is informed about these things, to whom also I speak with all freedom. For I am persuaded that of these things nothing is hidden from him; for this was not done in a corner.

title: Acts 26:27
text: King Agrippa, believest thou the prophets? I know that thou believest.

title: Acts 26:28
text: And Agrippa [said] to Paul, In a little thou persuadest me to become a Christian.

title: Acts 26:29
text: And Paul [said], I would to God, both in little and in much, that not only thou, but all who have heard me this day, should become such as *I* also am, except these bonds.

title: Acts 26:30
text: And the king stood up, and the governor and Bernice, and those who sat with them,

title: Acts 26:31
text: and having gone apart, they spoke to one another saying, This man does nothing worthy of death or of bonds.

title: Acts 26:32
text: And Agrippa said to Festus, This man might have been let go if he had not appealed to Caesar.

title: Acts 27:1
text: ¶But when it had been determined that we should sail to Italy, they delivered up Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion, by name Julius, of Augustus' company.

title: Acts 27:2
text: And going on board a ship of Adramyttium about to navigate by the places along Asia, we set sail, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.

title: Acts 27:3
text: And the next day we arrived at Sidon. And Julius treated Paul kindly and suffered him to go to his friends and refresh himself.

title: Acts 27:4
text: And setting sail thence we sailed under the lee of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.

title: Acts 27:5
text: And having sailed over the waters of Cilicia and Pamphylia we came to Myra in Lycia:

title: Acts 27:6
text: and there the centurion having found a ship of Alexandria sailing to Italy, he made us go on board her.

title: Acts 27:7
text: And sailing slowly for many days, and having with difficulty got abreast of Cnidus, the wind not suffering us, we sailed under the lee of Crete abreast of Salmone;

title: Acts 27:8
text: and coasting it with difficulty we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near to which was [the] city of Lasaea.

title: Acts 27:9
text: And much time having now been spent, and navigation being already dangerous, because the fast also was already past, Paul counselled them,

title: Acts 27:10
text: saying, Men, I perceive that the navigation will be with disaster and much loss, not only of the cargo and the ship, but also of our lives.

title: Acts 27:11
text: But the centurion believed rather the helmsman and the shipowner than what was said by Paul.

title: Acts 27:12
text: ¶And the harbour being ill adapted to winter in, the most counselled to set sail thence, if perhaps they might reach Phoenice to winter in, a port of Crete looking north-east and south-east.

title: Acts 27:13
text: And [the] south wind blowing gently, supposing that they had gained their object, having weighed anchor they sailed close in shore along Crete.

title: Acts 27:14
text: But not long after there came down it a hurricane called Euroclydon.

title: Acts 27:15
text: And the ship being caught and driven, and not able to bring her head to the wind, letting her go we were driven [before it].

title: Acts 27:16
text: But running under the lee of a certain island called Clauda, we were with difficulty able to make ourselves masters of the boat;

title: Acts 27:17
text: which having hoisted up, they used helps, frapping the ship; and fearing lest they should run into Syrtis and run aground, and having lowered the gear they were so driven.

title: Acts 27:18
text: But the storm being extremely violent on us, on the next day they threw cargo overboard,

title: Acts 27:19
text: and on the third day with their own hands they cast away the ship furniture.

title: Acts 27:20
text: And neither sun nor stars appearing for many days, and no small storm lying on us, in the end all hope of our being saved was taken away.

title: Acts 27:21
text: ¶And when they had been a long while without taking food, Paul then standing up in the midst of them said, Ye ought, O men, to have hearkened to me, and not have made sail from Crete and have gained this disaster and loss.

title: Acts 27:22
text: And now I exhort you to be of good courage, for there shall be no loss at all of life of [any] of you, only of the ship.

title: Acts 27:23
text: For an angel of the God, whose I am and whom I serve, stood by me this night,

title: Acts 27:24
text: saying, Fear not, Paul; thou must stand before Caesar; and behold, God has granted to thee all those that sail with thee.

title: Acts 27:25
text: Wherefore be of good courage, men, for I believe God that thus it shall be, as it has been said to me.

title: Acts 27:26
text: But we must be cast ashore on a certain island.

title: Acts 27:27
text: And when the fourteenth night was come, we being driven about in Adria, towards the middle of the night the sailors supposed that some land neared them,

title: Acts 27:28
text: and having sounded found twenty fathoms, and having gone a little farther and having again sounded they found fifteen fathoms;

title: Acts 27:29
text: and fearing lest we should be cast on rocky places, casting four anchors out of the stern, they wished that day were come.

title: Acts 27:30
text: But the sailors wishing to flee out of the ship, and having let down the boat into the sea under pretext of being about to carry out anchors from the prow,

title: Acts 27:31
text: Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, Unless these abide in the ship *ye* cannot be saved.

title: Acts 27:32
text: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the boat and let her fall.

title: Acts 27:33
text: And while it was drawing on to daylight, Paul exhorted them all to partake of food, saying, Ye have passed the fourteenth day watching in expectation without taking food.

title: Acts 27:34
text: Wherefore I exhort you to partake of food, for this has to do with your safety; for not a hair from the head of any one of you shall perish.

title: Acts 27:35
text: And, having said these things and taken a loaf, he gave thanks to God before all, and having broken it began to eat.

title: Acts 27:36
text: And all taking courage, themselves also took food.

title: Acts 27:37
text: And we were in the ship, all the souls, two hundred and seventy-six.

title: Acts 27:38
text: And having satisfied themselves with food, they lightened the ship, casting out the wheat into the sea.

title: Acts 27:39
text: And when it was day they did not recognise the land; but they perceived a certain bay having a strand, on which they were minded, if they should be able, to run the ship ashore;

title: Acts 27:40
text: and, having cast off the anchors, they left [them] in the sea, at the same time loosening the lashings of the rudders, and hoisting the foresail to the wind, they made for the strand.

title: Acts 27:41
text: And falling into a place where two seas met they ran the ship aground, and the prow having stuck itself fast remained unmoved, but the stern was broken by the force of the waves.

title: Acts 27:42
text: And [the] counsel of the soldiers was that they should kill the prisoners, lest any one should swim off and escape.

title: Acts 27:43
text: But the centurion, desirous of saving Paul, hindered them of their purpose, and commanded those who were able to swim, casting themselves first [into the sea], to get out on land;

title: Acts 27:44
text: and the rest, some on boards, some on some of the things [that came] from the ship; and thus it came to pass that all got safe to land.

title: Acts 28:1
text: ¶And when we got safe [to land] we then knew that the island was called Melita.

title: Acts 28:2
text: But the barbarians shewed us no common kindness; for, having kindled a fire, they took us all in because of the rain that was falling and because of the cold.

title: Acts 28:3
text: And Paul having gathered a [certain] quantity of sticks together in a bundle and laid [it] on the fire, a viper coming out from the heat seized his hand.

title: Acts 28:4
text: And when the barbarians saw the beast hanging from his hand, they said to one another, This man is certainly a murderer, whom, [though] saved out of the sea, Nemesis has not allowed to live.

title: Acts 28:5
text: *He* however, having shaken off the beast into the fire, felt no harm.

title: Acts 28:6
text: But *they* expected that he would have swollen or fallen down suddenly dead. But when they had expected a long time and saw nothing unusual happen to him, changing their opinion, they said he was a god.

title: Acts 28:7
text: Now in the country surrounding that place were the lands belonging to the chief man of the island, by name Publius, who received us and gave [us] hospitality three days in a very friendly way.

title: Acts 28:8
text: And it happened that the father of Publius lay ill of fever and dysentery; to whom Paul entered in, and having prayed and laid his hands on him cured him.

title: Acts 28:9
text: But this having taken place, the rest also who had sicknesses in the island came and were healed:

title: Acts 28:10
text: who also honoured us with many honours, and on our leaving they made presents to us of what should minister to our wants.

title: Acts 28:11
text: ¶And after three months we sailed in a ship which had wintered in the island, an Alexandrian, with [the] Dioscuri for its ensign.

title: Acts 28:12
text: And having come to Syracuse we remained three days.

title: Acts 28:13
text: Whence, going in a circuitous course, we arrived at Rhegium; and after one day, the wind having changed to south, on the second day we came to Puteoli,

title: Acts 28:14
text: where, having found brethren, we were begged to stay with them seven days. And thus we went to Rome.

title: Acts 28:15
text: And thence the brethren, having heard about us, came to meet us as far as Appii Forum and Tres Tabernae, whom when Paul saw, he thanked God and took courage.

title: Acts 28:16
text: And when we came to Rome, [the centurion delivered up the prisoners to the praetorian prefect, but] Paul was allowed to remain by himself with the soldier who kept him.

title: Acts 28:17
text: ¶And it came to pass after three days, that he called together those who were the chief of the Jews; and when they had come together he said to them, Brethren, *I* having done nothing against the people or the customs of our forefathers, have been delivered a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,

title: Acts 28:18
text: who having examined me were minded to let me go, because there was nothing worthy of death in me.

title: Acts 28:19
text: But the Jews speaking against it, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar, not as having anything to accuse my nation of.

title: Acts 28:20
text: For this cause therefore I have called you to [me] to see and to speak to you; for on account of the hope of Israel I have this chain about me.

title: Acts 28:21
text: And they said to him, For our part, we have neither received letters from Judaea concerning thee, nor has any one of the brethren who has arrived reported or said anything evil concerning thee.

title: Acts 28:22
text: But we beg to hear of thee what thou thinkest, for as concerning this sect it is known to us that it is everywhere spoken against.

title: Acts 28:23
text: ¶And having appointed him a day many came to him to the lodging, to whom he expounded, testifying of the kingdom of God, and persuading them concerning Jesus, both from the law of Moses and the prophets, from early morning to evening.

title: Acts 28:24
text: And some were persuaded of the things which were said, but some disbelieved.

title: Acts 28:25
text: And being disagreed among themselves they left; Paul having spoken one word, Well spoke the Holy Spirit through Esaias the prophet to our fathers,

title: Acts 28:26
text: saying, Go to this people, and say, Hearing ye shall hear and not understand, and seeing ye shall see and not perceive.

title: Acts 28:27
text: For the heart of this people has become fat, and they hear heavily with their ears, and they have closed their eyes; lest they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them.

title: Acts 28:28
text: Be it known to you therefore, that this salvation of God has been sent to the nations; *they* also will hear [it].

title: Acts 28:29
text: [And he having said this, the Jews went away, having great reasoning among themselves.]

title: Acts 28:30
text: ¶And he remained two whole years in his own hired lodging, and received all who came to him,

title: Acts 28:31
text: preaching the kingdom of God, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ, with all freedom unhinderedly.

title: Romans 1:1
text: ¶Paul, bondman of Jesus Christ, [a] called apostle, separated to God's glad tidings,

title: Romans 1:2
text: (which he had before promised by his prophets in holy writings,)

title: Romans 1:3
text: concerning his Son (come of David's seed according to flesh,

title: Romans 1:4
text: marked out Son of God in power, according to [the] Spirit of holiness, by resurrection of [the] dead) Jesus Christ our Lord;

title: Romans 1:5
text: by whom we have received grace and apostleship in behalf of his name, for obedience of faith among all the nations,

title: Romans 1:6
text: among whom are *ye* also [the] called of Jesus Christ:

title: Romans 1:7
text: to all that are in Rome, beloved of God, called saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and [our] Lord Jesus Christ.

title: Romans 1:8
text: ¶First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is proclaimed in the whole world.

title: Romans 1:9
text: For God is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the glad tidings of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you,

title: Romans 1:10
text: always beseeching at my prayers, if any way now at least I may be prospered by the will of God to come to you.

title: Romans 1:11
text: For I greatly desire to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to establish you;

title: Romans 1:12
text: that is, to have mutual comfort among you, each by the faith [which is] in the other, both yours and mine.

title: Romans 1:13
text: But I do not wish you to be ignorant, brethren, that I often proposed to come to you, (and have been hindered until the present time,) that I might have some fruit among you too, even as among the other nations also.

title: Romans 1:14
text: I am a debtor both to Greeks and barbarians, both to wise and unintelligent:

title: Romans 1:15
text: so, as far as depends on me, am I ready to announce the glad tidings to you also who [are] in Rome.

title: Romans 1:16
text: ¶For I am not ashamed of the glad tidings; for it is God's power to salvation, to every one that believes, both to Jew first and to Greek:

title: Romans 1:17
text: for righteousness of God is revealed therein, on the principle of faith, to faith: according as it is written, But the just shall live by faith.

title: Romans 1:18
text: For there is revealed wrath of God from heaven upon all impiety, and unrighteousness of men holding the truth in unrighteousness.

title: Romans 1:19
text: ¶Because what is known of God is manifest among them, for God has manifested [it] to them,

title: Romans 1:20
text: --for from [the] world's creation the invisible things of him are perceived, being apprehended by the mind through the things that are made, both his eternal power and divinity, --so as to render them inexcusable.

title: Romans 1:21
text: Because, knowing God, they glorified [him] not as God, neither were thankful; but fell into folly in their thoughts, and their heart without understanding was darkened:

title: Romans 1:22
text: professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

title: Romans 1:23
text: and changed the glory of the incorruptible God into [the] likeness of an image of corruptible man and of birds and quadrupeds and reptiles.

title: Romans 1:24
text: Wherefore God gave them up [also] in the lusts of their hearts to uncleanness, to dishonour their bodies between themselves:

title: Romans 1:25
text: who changed the truth of God into falsehood, and honoured and served the creature more than him who had created [it], who is blessed for ever. Amen.

title: Romans 1:26
text: For this reason God gave them up to vile lusts; for both their females changed the natural use into that contrary to nature;

title: Romans 1:27
text: and in like manner the males also, leaving the natural use of the female, were inflamed in their lust towards one another; males with males working shame, and receiving in themselves the recompense of their error which was fit.

title: Romans 1:28
text: And according as they did not think good to have God in [their] knowledge, God gave them up to a reprobate mind to practise unseemly things;

title: Romans 1:29
text: being filled with all unrighteousness, wickedness, covetousness, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, evil dispositions; whisperers,

title: Romans 1:30
text: back-biters, hateful to God, insolent, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,

title: Romans 1:31
text: void of understanding, faithless, without natural affection, unmerciful;

title: Romans 1:32
text: who knowing the righteous judgment of God, that they who do such things are worthy of death, not only practise them, but have fellow delight in those who do [them].

title: Romans 2:1
text: ¶Therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, every one who judgest, for in that in which thou judgest another, thou condemnest thyself; for thou that judgest doest the same things.

title: Romans 2:2
text: But we know that the judgment of God is according to truth upon those who do such things.

title: Romans 2:3
text: And thinkest thou this, O man, who judgest those that do such things, and practisest them [thyself], that *thou* shalt escape the judgment of God?

title: Romans 2:4
text: or despisest thou the riches of his goodness, and forbearance, and long-suffering, not knowing that the goodness of God leads thee to repentance?

title: Romans 2:5
text: but, according to thy hardness and impenitent heart, treasurest up to thyself wrath, in [the] day of wrath and revelation of [the] righteous judgment of God,

title: Romans 2:6
text: who shall render to each according to his works:

title: Romans 2:7
text: to them who, in patient continuance of good works, seek for glory and honour and incorruptibility, life eternal.

title: Romans 2:8
text: But to those that are contentious, and are disobedient to the truth, but obey unrighteousness, [there shall be] wrath and indignation,

title: Romans 2:9
text: tribulation and distress, on every soul of man that works evil, both of Jew first, and of Greek;

title: Romans 2:10
text: but glory and honour and peace to every one that works good, both to Jew first and to Greek:

title: Romans 2:11
text: for there is no acceptance of persons with God.

title: Romans 2:12
text: For as many as have sinned without law shall perish also without law; and as many as have sinned under law shall be judged by law,

title: Romans 2:13
text: (for not the hearers of the law [are] just before God, but the doers of the law shall be justified.

title: Romans 2:14
text: For when [those of the] nations, which have no law, practise by nature the things of the law, these, having no law, are a law to themselves;

title: Romans 2:15
text: who shew the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience also bearing witness, and their thoughts accusing or else excusing themselves between themselves;)

title: Romans 2:16
text: in [the] day when God shall judge the secrets of men, according to my glad tidings, by Jesus Christ.

title: Romans 2:17
text: ¶But if *thou* art named a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast in God,

title: Romans 2:18
text: and knowest the will, and discerningly approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law;

title: Romans 2:19
text: and hast confidence that thou thyself art a leader of the blind, a light of those who [are] in darkness,

title: Romans 2:20
text: an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, having the form of knowledge and of truth in the law:

title: Romans 2:21
text: thou then that teachest another, dost thou not teach thyself? thou that preachest not to steal, dost thou steal?

title: Romans 2:22
text: thou that sayest [man should] not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery? thou that abhorrest idols, dost thou commit sacrilege?

title: Romans 2:23
text: thou who boastest in law, dost thou by transgression of the law dishonour God?

title: Romans 2:24
text: For the name of God is blasphemed on your account among the nations, according as it is written.

title: Romans 2:25
text: For circumcision indeed profits if thou keep [the] law; but if thou be a law-transgressor, thy circumcision is become uncircumcision.

title: Romans 2:26
text: If therefore the uncircumcision keep the requirements of the law, shall not his uncircumcision be reckoned for circumcision,

title: Romans 2:27
text: and uncircumcision by nature, fulfilling the law, judge thee, who, with letter and circumcision, [art] a law-transgressor?

title: Romans 2:28
text: For he is not a Jew who [is] one outwardly, neither that circumcision which is outward in flesh;

title: Romans 2:29
text: but he [is] a Jew [who is so] inwardly; and circumcision, of the heart, in spirit, not in letter; whose praise [is] not of men, but of God.

title: Romans 3:1
text: ¶What then [is] the superiority of the Jew? or what the profit of circumcision?

title: Romans 3:2
text: Much every way: and first, indeed, that to them were entrusted the oracles of God.

title: Romans 3:3
text: For what? if some have not believed, shall their unbelief make the faith of God of none effect?

title: Romans 3:4
text: Far be the thought: but let God be true, and every man false; according as it is written, So that thou shouldest be justified in thy words, and shouldest overcome when thou art in judgment.

title: Romans 3:5
text: But if our unrighteousness commend God's righteousness, what shall we say? Is God unrighteous who inflicts wrath? I speak according to man.

title: Romans 3:6
text: Far be the thought: since how shall God judge the world?

title: Romans 3:7
text: For if the truth of God, in my lie, has more abounded to his glory, why yet am *I* also judged as a sinner?

title: Romans 3:8
text: and not, according as we are injuriously charged, and according as some affirm that we say, Let us practise evil things, that good ones may come? whose judgment is just.

title: Romans 3:9
text: What then? are we better? No, in no wise: for we have before charged both Jews and Greeks with being all under sin:

title: Romans 3:10
text: according as it is written, There is not a righteous [man], not even one;

title: Romans 3:11
text: there is not the [man] that understands, there is not one that seeks after God.

title: Romans 3:12
text: All have gone out of the way, they have together become unprofitable; there is not one that practises goodness, there is not so much as one:

title: Romans 3:13
text: their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have used deceit; asps' poison [is] under their lips:

title: Romans 3:14
text: whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness;

title: Romans 3:15
text: swift their feet to shed blood;

title: Romans 3:16
text: ruin and misery [are] in their ways,

title: Romans 3:17
text: and way of peace they have not known:

title: Romans 3:18
text: there is no fear of God before their eyes.

title: Romans 3:19
text: ¶Now we know that whatever the things the law says, it speaks to those under the law, that every mouth may be stopped, and all the world be under judgment to God.

title: Romans 3:20
text: Wherefore by works of law no flesh shall be justified before him; for by law [is] knowledge of sin.

title: Romans 3:21
text: But now without law righteousness of God is manifested, borne witness to by the law and the prophets;

title: Romans 3:22
text: righteousness of God by faith of Jesus Christ towards all, and upon all those who believe: for there is no difference;

title: Romans 3:23
text: for all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;

title: Romans 3:24
text: being justified freely by his grace through the redemption which [is] in Christ Jesus;

title: Romans 3:25
text: whom God has set forth a mercy-seat, through faith in his blood, for [the] shewing forth of his righteousness, in respect of the passing by the sins that had taken place before, through the forbearance of God;

title: Romans 3:26
text: for [the] shewing forth of his righteousness in the present time, so that he should be just, and justify him that is of [the] faith of Jesus.

title: Romans 3:27
text: Where then [is] boasting? It has been excluded. By what law? of works? Nay, but by law of faith;

title: Romans 3:28
text: for we reckon that a man is justified by faith, without works of law.

title: Romans 3:29
text: Is [God] the God of Jews only? is he not of [the] nations also? Yea, of nations also:

title: Romans 3:30
text: since indeed [it is] one God who shall justify [the] circumcision on the principle of faith, and uncircumcision by faith.

title: Romans 3:31
text: Do we then make void law by faith? Far be the thought: [no,] but we establish law.

title: Romans 4:1
text: ¶What shall we say then that Abraham our father according to flesh has found?

title: Romans 4:2
text: For if Abraham has been justified on the principle of works, he has whereof to boast: but not before God;

title: Romans 4:3
text: for what does the scripture say? And Abraham believed God, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.

title: Romans 4:4
text: Now to him that works the reward is not reckoned as of grace, but of debt:

title: Romans 4:5
text: but to him who does not work, but believes on him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is reckoned as righteousness.

title: Romans 4:6
text: Even as David also declares the blessedness of the man to whom God reckons righteousness without works:

title: Romans 4:7
text: Blessed [they] whose lawlessnesses have been forgiven, and whose sins have been covered:

title: Romans 4:8
text: blessed [the] man to whom [the] Lord shall not at all reckon sin.

title: Romans 4:9
text: ¶[Does] this blessedness then [rest] on the circumcision, or also on the uncircumcision? For we say that faith has been reckoned to Abraham as righteousness.

title: Romans 4:10
text: How then has it been reckoned? when he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not in circumcision, but in uncircumcision.

title: Romans 4:11
text: And he received [the] sign of circumcision [as] seal of the righteousness of faith which [he had] being in uncircumcision, that he might be [the] father of all them that believe being in uncircumcision, that righteousness might be reckoned to them also;

title: Romans 4:12
text: and father of circumcision, not only to those who are of [the] circumcision, but to those also who walk in the steps of the faith, during uncircumcision, of our father Abraham.

title: Romans 4:13
text: For [it was] not by law that the promise was to Abraham, or to his seed, that he should be heir of [the] world, but by righteousness of faith.

title: Romans 4:14
text: For if they which [are] of law be heirs, faith is made vain, and the promise made of no effect.

title: Romans 4:15
text: For law works wrath; but where no law is neither [is there] transgression.

title: Romans 4:16
text: Therefore [it is] on the principle of faith, that [it might be] according to grace, in order to the promise being sure to all the seed, not to that only which [is] of the law, but to that also which [is] of Abraham's faith, who is father of us all,

title: Romans 4:17
text: ¶(according as it is written, I have made thee father of many nations,) before the God whom he believed, who quickens the dead, and calls the things which be not as being;

title: Romans 4:18
text: who against hope believed in hope to his becoming father of many nations, according to that which was spoken, So shall thy seed be:

title: Romans 4:19
text: and not being weak in faith, he considered not his own body already become dead, being about a hundred years old, and the deadening of Sarah's womb,

title: Romans 4:20
text: and hesitated not at the promise of God through unbelief; but found strength in faith, giving glory to God;

title: Romans 4:21
text: and being fully persuaded that what he has promised he is able also to do;

title: Romans 4:22
text: wherefore also it was reckoned to him as righteousness.

title: Romans 4:23
text: ¶Now it was not written on his account alone that it was reckoned to him,

title: Romans 4:24
text: but on ours also, to whom, believing on him who has raised from among [the] dead Jesus our Lord,

title: Romans 4:25
text: who has been delivered for our offences and has been raised for our justification, it will be reckoned.

title: Romans 5:1
text: ¶Therefore having been justified on the principle of faith, we have peace towards God through our Lord Jesus Christ;

title: Romans 5:2
text: by whom we have also access by faith into this favour in which we stand, and we boast in hope of the glory of God.

title: Romans 5:3
text: And not only [that], but we also boast in tribulations, knowing that tribulation works endurance;

title: Romans 5:4
text: and endurance, experience; and experience, hope;

title: Romans 5:5
text: and hope does not make ashamed, because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by [the] Holy Spirit which has been given to us:

title: Romans 5:6
text: ¶for we being still without strength, in [the] due time Christ has died for [the] ungodly.

title: Romans 5:7
text: For scarcely for [the] just [man] will one die, for perhaps for [the] good [man] some one might also dare to die;

title: Romans 5:8
text: but God commends *his* love to us, in that, we being still sinners, Christ has died for us.

title: Romans 5:9
text: Much rather therefore, having been now justified in [the power of] his blood, we shall be saved by him from wrath.

title: Romans 5:10
text: For if, being enemies, we have been reconciled to God through the death of his Son, much rather, having been reconciled, we shall be saved in [the power of] his life.

title: Romans 5:11
text: And not only [that], but [we are] making our boast in God, through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom now we have received the reconciliation.

title: Romans 5:12
text: For this [cause], even as by one man sin entered into the world, and by sin death; and thus death passed upon all men, for that all have sinned:

title: Romans 5:13
text: (for until law sin was in [the] world; but sin is not put to account when there is no law;

title: Romans 5:14
text: but death reigned from Adam until Moses, even upon those who had not sinned in the likeness of Adam's transgression, who is [the] figure of him to come.

title: Romans 5:15
text: But [shall] not the act of favour [be] as the offence? For if by the offence of one the many have died, much rather has the grace of God, and the free gift in grace, which [is] by the one man Jesus Christ, abounded unto the many.

title: Romans 5:16
text: And [shall] not as by one that has sinned [be] the gift? For the judgment [was] of one to condemnation, but the act of favour, of many offences unto justification.

title: Romans 5:17
text: For if by the offence of the one death reigned by the one, much rather shall those who receive the abundance of grace, and of the free gift of righteousness, reign in life by the one Jesus Christ:)

title: Romans 5:18
text: so then as [it was] by one offence towards all men to condemnation, so by one righteousness towards all men for justification of life.

title: Romans 5:19
text: For as indeed by the disobedience of the one man the many have been constituted sinners, so also by the obedience of the one the many will be constituted righteous.

title: Romans 5:20
text: But law came in, in order that the offence might abound; but where sin abounded grace has overabounded,

title: Romans 5:21
text: in order that, even as sin has reigned in [the power of] death, so also grace might reign through righteousness to eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.

title: Romans 6:1
text: ¶What then shall we say? Should we continue in sin that grace may abound?

title: Romans 6:2
text: Far be the thought. We who have died to sin, how shall we still live in it?

title: Romans 6:3
text: Are you ignorant that we, as many as have been baptised unto Christ Jesus, have been baptised unto his death?

title: Romans 6:4
text: We have been buried therefore with him by baptism unto death, in order that, even as Christ has been raised up from among [the] dead by the glory of the Father, so *we* also should walk in newness of life.

title: Romans 6:5
text: For if we are become identified with [him] in the likeness of his death, so also we shall be of [his] resurrection;

title: Romans 6:6
text: knowing this, that our old man has been crucified with [him], that the body of sin might be annulled, that we should no longer serve sin.

title: Romans 6:7
text: For he that has died is justified from sin.

title: Romans 6:8
text: Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we shall also live with him,

title: Romans 6:9
text: knowing that Christ having been raised up from among [the] dead dies no more: death has dominion over him no more.

title: Romans 6:10
text: For in that he has died, he has died to sin once for all; but in that he lives, he lives to God.

title: Romans 6:11
text: So also *ye*, reckon yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus.

title: Romans 6:12
text: Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body to obey its lusts.

title: Romans 6:13
text: Neither yield your members instruments of unrighteousness to sin, but yield yourselves to God as alive from among [the] dead, and your members instruments of righteousness to God.

title: Romans 6:14
text: For sin shall not have dominion over *you*, for ye are not under law but under grace.

title: Romans 6:15
text: What then? should we sin because we are not under law but under grace? Far be the thought.

title: Romans 6:16
text: Know ye not that to whom ye yield yourselves bondmen for obedience, ye are bondmen to him whom ye obey, whether of sin unto death, or of obedience unto righteousness?

title: Romans 6:17
text: But thanks [be] to God, that ye were bondmen of sin, but have obeyed from the heart the form of teaching into which ye were instructed.

title: Romans 6:18
text: Now, having got your freedom from sin, ye have become bondmen to righteousness.

title: Romans 6:19
text: I speak humanly on account of the weakness of your flesh. For even as ye have yielded your members in bondage to uncleanness and to lawlessness unto lawlessness, so now yield your members in bondage to righteousness unto holiness.

title: Romans 6:20
text: For when ye were bondmen of sin ye were free from righteousness.

title: Romans 6:21
text: What fruit therefore had ye *then* in the things of which ye are *now* ashamed? for the end of *them* [is] death.

title: Romans 6:22
text: But *now*, having got your freedom from sin, and having become bondmen to God, ye have your fruit unto holiness, and the end eternal life.

title: Romans 6:23
text: For the wages of sin [is] death; but the act of favour of God, eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

title: Romans 7:1
text: ¶Are ye ignorant, brethren, (for I speak to those knowing law,) that law rules over a man as long as he lives?

title: Romans 7:2
text: For the married woman is bound by law to her husband so long as he is alive; but if the husband should die, she is clear from the law of the husband:

title: Romans 7:3
text: so then, the husband being alive, she shall be called an adulteress if she be to another man; but if the husband should die, she is free from the law, so as not to be an adulteress, though she be to another man.

title: Romans 7:4
text: So that, my brethren, *ye* also have been made dead to the law by the body of the Christ, to be to another, who has been raised up from among [the] dead, in order that we might bear fruit to God.

title: Romans 7:5
text: For when we were in the flesh the passions of sins, which [were] by the law, wrought in our members to bring forth fruit to death;

title: Romans 7:6
text: but now we are clear from the law, having died in that in which we were held, so that we should serve in newness of spirit, and not in oldness of letter.

title: Romans 7:7
text: ¶What shall we say then? [is] the law sin? Far be the thought. But I had not known sin, unless by law: for I had not had conscience also of lust unless the law had said, Thou shalt not lust;

title: Romans 7:8
text: but sin, getting a point of attack by the commandment, wrought in me every lust; for without law sin [was] dead.

title: Romans 7:9
text: But *I* was alive without law once; but the commandment having come, sin revived, but *I* died.

title: Romans 7:10
text: And the commandment, which [was] for life, was found, [as] to me, itself [to be] unto death:

title: Romans 7:11
text: for sin, getting a point of attack by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew [me].

title: Romans 7:12
text: So that the law indeed [is] holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.

title: Romans 7:13
text: Did then that which is good become death to me? Far be the thought. But sin, that it might appear sin, working death to me by that which is good; in order that sin by the commandment might become exceeding sinful.

title: Romans 7:14
text: ¶For we know that the law is spiritual: but *I* am fleshly, sold under sin.

title: Romans 7:15
text: For that which I do, I do not own: for not what I will, this I do; but what I hate, this I practise.

title: Romans 7:16
text: But if what I do not will, this I practise, I consent to the law that [it is] right.

title: Romans 7:17
text: Now then [it is] no longer *I* [that] do it, but the sin that dwells in me.

title: Romans 7:18
text: For I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, good does not dwell: for to will is there with me, but to do right [I find] not.

title: Romans 7:19
text: For I do not practise the good that I will; but the evil I do not will, that I do.

title: Romans 7:20
text: But if what *I* do not will, this I practise, [it is] no longer *I* [that] do it, but the sin that dwells in me.

title: Romans 7:21
text: I find then the law upon *me* who will to practise what is right, that with *me* evil is there.

title: Romans 7:22
text: For I delight in the law of God according to the inward man:

title: Romans 7:23
text: but I see another law in my members, warring in opposition to the law of my mind, and bringing me into captivity to the law of sin which exists in my members.

title: Romans 7:24
text: O wretched man that I [am]! who shall deliver me out of this body of death?

title: Romans 7:25
text: I thank God, through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then *I* *myself* with the mind serve God's law; but with the flesh sin's law.

title: Romans 8:1
text: ¶[There is] then now no condemnation to those in Christ Jesus.

title: Romans 8:2
text: For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and of death.

title: Romans 8:3
text: For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God, having sent his own Son, in likeness of flesh of sin, and for sin, has condemned sin in the flesh,

title: Romans 8:4
text: in order that the righteous requirement of the law should be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to flesh but according to Spirit.

title: Romans 8:5
text: For they that are according to flesh mind the things of the flesh; and they that are according to Spirit, the things of the Spirit.

title: Romans 8:6
text: For the mind of the flesh [is] death; but the mind of the Spirit life and peace.

title: Romans 8:7
text: Because the mind of the flesh is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God; for neither indeed can it be:

title: Romans 8:8
text: and they that are in flesh cannot please God.

title: Romans 8:9
text: But *ye* are not in flesh but in Spirit, if indeed God's Spirit dwell in you; but if any one has not [the] Spirit of Christ *he* is not of him:

title: Romans 8:10
text: ¶but if Christ be in you, the body is dead on account of sin, but the Spirit life on account of righteousness.

title: Romans 8:11
text: But if the Spirit of him that has raised up Jesus from among [the] dead dwell in you, he that has raised up Christ from among [the] dead shall quicken your mortal bodies also on account of his Spirit which dwells in you.

title: Romans 8:12
text: So then, brethren, we are debtors, not to the flesh, to live according to flesh;

title: Romans 8:13
text: for if ye live according to flesh, ye are about to die; but if, by the Spirit, ye put to death the deeds of the body, ye shall live:

title: Romans 8:14
text: for as many as are led by [the] Spirit of God, *these* are sons of God.

title: Romans 8:15
text: For ye have not received a spirit of bondage again for fear, but ye have received a spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father.

title: Romans 8:16
text: The Spirit itself bears witness with our spirit, that we are children of God.

title: Romans 8:17
text: ¶And if children, heirs also: heirs of God, and Christ's joint heirs; if indeed we suffer with [him], that we may also be glorified with [him].

title: Romans 8:18
text: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy [to be compared] with the coming glory to be revealed to us.

title: Romans 8:19
text: For the anxious looking out of the creature expects the revelation of the sons of God:

title: Romans 8:20
text: for the creature has been made subject to vanity, not of its will, but by reason of him who has subjected [the same], in hope

title: Romans 8:21
text: that the creature itself also shall be set free from the bondage of corruption into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.

title: Romans 8:22
text: For we know that the whole creation groans together and travails in pain together until now.

title: Romans 8:23
text: And not only [that], but even *we* ourselves, who have the first-fruits of the Spirit, we also ourselves groan in ourselves, awaiting adoption, [that is] the redemption of our body.

title: Romans 8:24
text: For we have been saved in hope; but hope seen is not hope; for what any one sees, why does he also hope?

title: Romans 8:25
text: But if what we see not we hope, we expect in patience.

title: Romans 8:26
text: ¶And in like manner the Spirit joins also its help to our weakness; for we do not know what we should pray for as is fitting, but the Spirit itself makes intercession with groanings which cannot be uttered.

title: Romans 8:27
text: But he who searches the hearts knows what [is] the mind of the Spirit, because he intercedes for saints according to God.

title: Romans 8:28
text: But we *do* know that all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are called according to purpose.

title: Romans 8:29
text: ¶Because whom he has foreknown, he has also predestinated [to be] conformed to the image of his Son, so that he should be [the] firstborn among many brethren.

title: Romans 8:30
text: But whom he has predestinated, these also he has called; and whom he has called, these also he has justified; but whom he has justified, these also he has glorified.

title: Romans 8:31
text: ¶What shall we then say to these things? If God [be] for us, who against us?

title: Romans 8:32
text: He who, yea, has not spared his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not also with him grant us all things?

title: Romans 8:33
text: Who shall bring an accusation against God's elect? [It is] God who justifies:

title: Romans 8:34
text: who is he that condemns? [It is] Christ who has died, but rather has been [also] raised up; who is also at the right hand of God; who also intercedes for us.

title: Romans 8:35
text: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? tribulation or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?

title: Romans 8:36
text: According as it is written, For thy sake we are put to death all the day long; we have been reckoned as sheep for slaughter.

title: Romans 8:37
text: But in all these things we more than conquer through him that has loved us.

title: Romans 8:38
text: For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers,

title: Romans 8:39
text: nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which [is] in Christ Jesus our Lord.

title: Romans 9:1
text: ¶I say [the] truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience bearing witness with me in [the] Holy Spirit,

title: Romans 9:2
text: that I have great grief and uninterrupted pain in my heart,

title: Romans 9:3
text: for I have wished, I myself, to be a curse from the Christ for my brethren, my kinsmen, according to flesh;

title: Romans 9:4
text: who are Israelites; whose [is] the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants, and the law-giving, and the service, and the promises;

title: Romans 9:5
text: whose [are] the fathers; and of whom, as according to flesh, [is] the Christ, who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.

title: Romans 9:6
text: ¶Not however as though the word of God had failed; for not all [are] Israel which [are] of Israel;

title: Romans 9:7
text: nor because they are seed of Abraham [are] all children: but, In Isaac shall a seed be called to thee.

title: Romans 9:8
text: That is, [they that are] the children of the flesh, these [are] not the children of God; but the children of the promise are reckoned as seed.

title: Romans 9:9
text: For this word [is] of promise, According to this time I will come, and there shall be a son to Sarah.

title: Romans 9:10
text: And not only [that], but Rebecca having conceived by one, Isaac our father,

title: Romans 9:11
text: [the children] indeed being not yet born, or having done anything good or worthless (that the purpose of God according to election might abide, not of works, but of him that calls),

title: Romans 9:12
text: it was said to her, The greater shall serve the less:

title: Romans 9:13
text: according as it is written, I have loved Jacob, and I have hated Esau.

title: Romans 9:14
text: ¶What shall we say then? [Is there] unrighteousness with God? Far be the thought.

title: Romans 9:15
text: For he says to Moses, I will shew mercy to whom I will shew mercy, and I will feel compassion for whom I will feel compassion.

title: Romans 9:16
text: So then [it is] not of him that wills, nor of him that runs, but of God that shews mercy.

title: Romans 9:17
text: For the scripture says to Pharaoh, For this very thing I have raised thee up from amongst [men], that I might thus shew in thee my power, and so that my name should be declared in all the earth.

title: Romans 9:18
text: So then, to whom he will he shews mercy, and whom he will he hardens.

title: Romans 9:19
text: Thou wilt say to me then, Why does he yet find fault? for who resists his purpose?

title: Romans 9:20
text: Aye, but thou, O man, who art *thou* that answerest again to God? Shall the thing formed say to him that has formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?

title: Romans 9:21
text: Or has not the potter authority over the clay, out of the same lump to make one vessel to honour, and another to dishonour?

title: Romans 9:22
text: And if God, minded to shew his wrath and to make his power known, endured with much long-suffering vessels of wrath fitted for destruction;

title: Romans 9:23
text: and that he might make known the riches of his glory upon vessels of mercy, which he had before prepared for glory,

title: Romans 9:24
text: us, whom he has also called, not only from amongst [the] Jews, but also from amongst [the] nations?

title: Romans 9:25
text: ¶As he says also in Hosea, I will call not-my-people My people; and the-not-beloved Beloved.

title: Romans 9:26
text: And it shall be, in the place where it was said to them, *Ye* [are] not my people, there shall they be called Sons of [the] living God.

title: Romans 9:27
text: But Esaias cries concerning Israel, Should the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, the remnant shall be saved:

title: Romans 9:28
text: for [he] is bringing the matter to an end, and [cutting [it] short in righteousness; because] a cutting short of the matter will [the] Lord accomplish upon the earth.

title: Romans 9:29
text: And according as Esaias said before, Unless [the] Lord of hosts had left us a seed, we had been as Sodom, and made like even as Gomorrha.

title: Romans 9:30
text: ¶What then shall we say? That [they of the] nations, who did not follow after righteousness, have attained righteousness, but [the] righteousness that is on the principle of faith.

title: Romans 9:31
text: But Israel, pursuing after a law of righteousness, has not attained to [that] law.

title: Romans 9:32
text: Wherefore? Because [it was] not on the principle of faith, but as of works. They have stumbled at the stumblingstone,

title: Romans 9:33
text: according as it is written, Behold, I place in Zion a stone of stumbling and rock of offence: and he that believes on him shall not be ashamed.

title: Romans 10:1
text: ¶Brethren, the delight of my own heart and my supplication which [I address] to God for them is for salvation.

title: Romans 10:2
text: For I bear them witness that they have zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.

title: Romans 10:3
text: For they, being ignorant of God's righteousness, and seeking to establish their own [righteousness], have not submitted to the righteousness of God.

title: Romans 10:4
text: For Christ is [the] end of law for righteousness to every one that believes.

title: Romans 10:5
text: For Moses lays down in writing the righteousness which is of the law, The man who has practised those things shall live by them.

title: Romans 10:6
text: But the righteousness of faith speaks thus: Do not say in thine heart, Who shall ascend to the heavens? that is, to bring Christ down;

title: Romans 10:7
text: or, Who shall descend into the abyss? that is, to bring up Christ from among [the] dead.

title: Romans 10:8
text: But what says it? The word is near thee, in thy mouth and in thy heart: that is, the word of faith, which we preach:

title: Romans 10:9
text: that if thou shalt confess with thy mouth Jesus as Lord, and shalt believe in thine heart that God has raised him from among [the] dead, thou shalt be saved.

title: Romans 10:10
text: For with [the] heart is believed to righteousness; and with [the] mouth confession made to salvation.

title: Romans 10:11
text: For the scripture says, No one believing on him shall be ashamed.

title: Romans 10:12
text: ¶For there is no difference of Jew and Greek; for the same Lord of all [is] rich towards all that call upon him.

title: Romans 10:13
text: For every one whosoever, who shall call on the name of the Lord, shall be saved.

title: Romans 10:14
text: How then shall they call upon him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe on him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without one who preaches?

title: Romans 10:15
text: and how shall they preach unless they have been sent? according as it is written, How beautiful the feet of them that announce glad tidings of peace, of them that announce glad tidings of good things!

title: Romans 10:16
text: But they have not all obeyed the glad tidings. For Esaias says, Lord, who has believed our report?

title: Romans 10:17
text: So faith then [is] by a report, but the report by God's word.

title: Romans 10:18
text: But I say, Have they not heard? Yea, surely, Their voice has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the extremities of the habitable world.

title: Romans 10:19
text: But I say, Has not Israel known? First, Moses says, *I* will provoke you to jealousy through [them that are] not a nation: through a nation without understanding I will anger you.

title: Romans 10:20
text: But Esaias is very bold, and says, I have been found by those not seeking me; I have become manifest to those not inquiring after me.

title: Romans 10:21
text: But unto Israel he says, All the day long I have stretched out my hands unto a people disobeying and opposing.

title: Romans 11:1
text: ¶I say then, Has God cast away his people? Far be the thought. For *I* also am an Israelite, of [the] seed of Abraham, of [the] tribe of Benjamin.

title: Romans 11:2
text: God has not cast away his people whom he foreknew. Know ye not what the scripture says in [the history of] Elias, how he pleads with God against Israel?

title: Romans 11:3
text: Lord, they have killed thy prophets, they have dug down thine altars; and *I* have been left alone, and they seek my life.

title: Romans 11:4
text: But what says the divine answer to him? I have left to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed knee to Baal.

title: Romans 11:5
text: Thus, then, in the present time also there has been a remnant according to election of grace.

title: Romans 11:6
text: But if by grace, no longer of works: since [otherwise] grace is no more grace.

title: Romans 11:7
text: What [is it] then? What Israel seeks for, that he has not obtained; but the election has obtained, and the rest have been blinded,

title: Romans 11:8
text: according as it is written, God has given to them a spirit of slumber, eyes not to see, and ears not to hear, unto this day.

title: Romans 11:9
text: And David says, Let their table be for a snare, and for a gin, and for a fall-trap, and for a recompense to them:

title: Romans 11:10
text: let their eyes be darkened not to see, and bow down their back alway.

title: Romans 11:11
text: I say then, Have they stumbled in order that they might fall? Far be the thought: but by their fall [there is] salvation to the nations to provoke them to jealousy.

title: Romans 11:12
text: But if their fall [be the] world's wealth, and their loss [the] wealth of [the] nations, how much rather their fulness?

title: Romans 11:13
text: For I speak to you, the nations, inasmuch as *I* am apostle of nations, I glorify my ministry;

title: Romans 11:14
text: if by any means I shall provoke to jealousy [them which are] my flesh, and shall save some from among them.

title: Romans 11:15
text: For if their casting away [be the] world's reconciliation, what [their] reception but life from among [the] dead?
